approachQuestion.prompt: A read-only R by C rectangular grid contains integer travel charges. Starting at the top-left, reach the bottom-right using only right or down moves. Pay for every visited cell, including endpoints. Return the minimum total charge. Examples: [[1,9],[2,3]] → 6; [[-2,4,-3]] → -1. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 1 ≤ R,C ≤ 1000; −1000 ≤ charge ≤ 1000. There are no blocked cells. Return only a signed 64-bit total.

options.text: Keep C minimum costs. Scan row by row, left to right. Initialize the start from its charge, handle the first row and first column using their sole predecessor, and elsewhere add the current charge to the smaller of the old column cost and updated left cost.
options.feedback: Every route enters from above or left. Negative charges are safe because moves never form cycles; the two incoming prefix optima exhaust legal predecessors.

options.text: Compute the same minimum for each cell but retain the full R by C table.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: At every cell move to the cheaper immediately adjacent legal cell until reaching the destination.
options.feedback: For [[0,1,100],[2,100,100],[2,2,0]], right is locally cheaper, but every route starting right costs at least 103. Down-down-right-right costs 6.

options.text: Return the sum of the smallest charge in each row.
options.feedback: For [[1,100],[100,1]], this returns 2 but every legal route costs 102.

feedback.reason: Minimize arrival costs on an acyclic grid even when local charges can be negative.
details: Allocate C costs and scan all RC cells, updating the minimum arrival cost in place using above and left. Handle row and column boundaries explicitly; do not copy rows.

Each arrival cost adds the current charge to the smaller valid predecessor from above or left. Boundary cells have fewer predecessors, not extra zero-cost routes. One row suffices because only the final cost is requested.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Allocate C costs and scan all RC cells, updating the minimum arrival cost in place using above and left. Handle row and column boundaries explicitly; do not copy rows. Analyze this fixed implementation. N=RC; R,C vary independently. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: Every cell updates one entry of a C-sized cost row.
details: Every cell does constant work, and initializing C costs is dominated by RC. One C-entry row is live. No paths, heap, recursion, hashing, or copies are used.
“O(R+C) time, O(C) auxiliary space”: The method visits every cell; it does not trace just one route along a row and column.
“O(RC) time, O(RC) auxiliary space”: The fixed method overwrites one C-entry row rather than retaining the whole cost grid.
“O(RC) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The C allocated arrival costs grow with the number of columns.
